hints: Consider particle $B$ hanging freely in equilibrium: the tension in the string equals the weight of $B$, so $T = m_B g$.
Consider particle $A$ on the smooth inclined plane in equilibrium: the tension $T$ balances the component of weight acting down the slope, $T = m_A g \sin\theta$.
Equate the two expressions for tension and solve for $\sin\theta$ and $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces vertically for the hanging particle $B$ in equilibrium with $m_B = 0.2\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T = m_B g = 0.2(10) = 2\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces parallel to the smooth inclined plane for particle $A$ in equilibrium with $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$:
$$T = m_A g\sin\theta = 0.4(10)\sin\theta = 4\sin\theta$$

Equate the expressions for tension $T$ to solve for $\theta$:
$$4\sin\theta = 2$$
$$\sin\theta = \frac{2}{4} = 0.5$$
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough: Analyze the equilibrium of the two connected particles separately. The pulley is smooth and light, so the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the string.

For particle $B$ of mass $m_B = 0.2\text{ kg}$, it hangs vertically at rest. Set the upward tension equal to its downward weight:
$$T = m_B g$$
Substitute $m_B = 0.2\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T = 0.2 \times 10 = 2\text{ N}$$

For particle $A$ of mass $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$, the plane is smooth (no friction). The forces along the inclined plane are the tension $T$ pulling up the plane and the component of weight acting down the plane:
$$T - m_A g\sin\theta = 0$$
$$T = m_A g\sin\theta$$
Substitute $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T = 0.4 \times 10 \times \sin\theta = 4\sin\theta$$

Substitute $T = 2\text{ N}$ into the equation for $A$:
$$4\sin\theta = 2$$
Divide both sides by $4$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{2}{4} = 0.5$$
Take the inverse sine:
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^\circ$$
Thus the angle of the incline is $30^\circ$.

hints: Resolve particle $B$ downwards and particle $A$ up the smooth plane using $F=ma$.
Add the two equations to eliminate the tension, then substitute the acceleration back to find $T$.
The particles begin at rest and move $0.5\text{ m}$ before $B$ reaches the ground.
Use $v^2=u^2+2as$ with the acceleration from part (ii)(a).
walkthrough: Therefore $v=1.03\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to 3 significant figures.

hints: After $B$ reaches the ground, the string is slack and $A$ travels freely up the smooth plane.
Set the loss of kinetic energy equal to the gain of gravitational potential energy, then add the first $0.5\text{ m}$.
walkthrough: This gives $d=0.154\text{ m}$, so the total distance is $0.5+0.154=0.654\text{ m}$.
